about.title: Banning Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Banning residents rely on all kinds of consumer products, tools, vehicle parts, and household equipment every day, and most of the time these items work as expected. But when a product has a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or an inadequate warning, the results can be serious. California law generally applies strict liability to these cases, meaning an injured person doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. That standard can apply to the manufacturer, distributor, or retailer involved in getting the product to market. If a defective product has hurt you or someone in your family in Banning, keeping the item itself, along with packaging and receipts, matters a great deal for building a claim. LawProactive connects injured Banning residents with an independent attorney, free of charge, so you can understand your options without guesswork.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Your Claim

items.title: You Don't Have to Prove Negligence
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, an injured person generally only needs to show the product was defective and caused harm, not that anyone was careless.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable under this framework, which can widen the paths available for pursuing a claim.

items.title: Preserving the Product Is Critical
items.desc: Since the defect itself is central to a strict liability claim, keeping the product, its packaging, and any related paperwork intact can meaningfully affect the strength of a case.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, which focuses on whether the product itself was defective and caused injury, not on the manufacturer's level of care. This can make these claims different from typical negligence-based injury cases.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep the product exactly as it was at the time of the incident, along with any packaging, manuals, or receipts. Don't attempt repairs or alterations, since the product's condition can be important evidence in a strict liability claim.
